chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
«It is appropriate for the Imam to make the Tashahhud audible to those behind him, and they should not make anything audible to him.»

key_terms.التَّشَهُّد: The Tashahhud (testimony of faith recited in prayer)
key_terms.يُسْمِع: To make audible / to cause to hear

ai.seo_question: Should the Imam recite the Tashahjud aloud during prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the procedural distinction between the Imam and the congregation during the final sitting of prayer, emphasizing the Imam's role as the audible leader. It reflects the Shia jurisprudential view that the congregation listens attentively to the Imam's recitation of the Tashahhud rather than reciting it themselves, ensuring unity and order in the ritual. This ruling underscores the hierarchical structure of congregational prayer where the Imam's actions set the standard for the followers.
